doc.title: Paul Shaffer interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 24, 2023

title: Playing the promo man in 'This Is Spinal Tap'
summary: Harry Shearer got him the role; he describes the improvised scenes, cut key scene and the 'Kick my ass' meltdown.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: Did you have to audition for the role in “Spinal Tap”?

No. Harry Shearer got me that role and just sold me to the other guys. And, ‘cause we had been on the fifth year of SNL together, both of us having offices near each other and collaborated on some musical things. And we are friends to this day. And he just said, “Paul, this guy is funny and you should use him in this part” the local promo man. And they said okay. Rob bought it. And they all knew me to varying degrees. Chris more so, Chris Guest, he and I did early National Lampoon songs together, ’74.
Did the tape, did the scene take a lot of time to film?
Oh. Well I did two days’ work on this film. Some of my — my key scene really was cut from the film and it wasn’t really my fault it was because another scene didn’t work out

and this scene depended on it. Luckily on the DVD you can see it as a bonus scene. But they just sort of made an effort to leave me in as much as they could once they had cut my key scene. But between all my various scenes, one was in a record store that they did leave in, the in-store signing, and then some remnants of the one the night before where I have to talk them into going to a radio station and then we had to cut the radio station. Two days work on the film. All different — you know no written lines though. I said to Harry when he told me about it and I said, “So you’ll send me my lines then.” And he said, “You’ll be making them up.” And he meant it. There were scene outlines but no dialogue written. So in my case, you know just coming out for two days, I had to learn the various names of the characters and a lot of the backstories too, what’s the president of the label Sir Ian you know and the different names that I would have to quote sometimes.
Did you guys get that from Ahmet Ertegun from Atlantic Records, did you think that that was like an appropriate?
Well I’m not sure, you know I’m not sure where they got Sir Ian.
Yeah. Oh that’s what I said, Sir Ian, yeah.
I think Tony Hendra, who was a British actor himself, played Sir Ian or whomever, and whenever they could they liked to get real British accents in.
Well weren’t you begging them to kick you in the butt?

That’s right, now kick my ass was my key scene in that, in store. The in-store records. A promo man, I was a promo man who was set up and in store but no one came. And not only that the records were all black, the covers. You couldn’t see the black felt markers to sign them. Everything went wrong. And this guy has a meltdown, the promo man. And apparently it was based on a real promo man. And when these Spinal Tap members once had a comedy record out they had a promo man who did this, had a meltdown and said, “Kick my ass it’s my fault.” And so I knew, you know, this scene by when we got to the end of it that’s where it has to go.
